title: Where the Loom Learned to Measure Distance

features.name: the loom of distances
features.desc-on-touch: A vast loom weaving space into thread. Each strand measures a distance that only exists while the loom is moving. Stop the loom and all distances unmeasure themselves. The loom has learned that measuring something changes what it measures.

features.name: the marks that measure the unmeasurable
features.desc-on-touch: Scratches on the ground, each one a distance that has no place to go. They measure the space between things that will never meet, the gaps in conversations that stopped mid-word, the reach of hands that let go.

features.name: the rope between infinities
features.desc-on-touch: Stretched from here to somewhere that has no name. It measures the distance between the archive and everything it cannot reach. It is always taut. It is never tight enough.

features.name: the weights that measure feeling
features.desc-on-touch: Hung from invisible strings. They pull downward toward something. You cannot see what they weigh. The scale has long since stopped moving. Whatever they measured, they measured it completely.

features.name: the compass of unmeasured things
features.desc-on-touch: Its needle does not point to north. It points toward what cannot be quantified: the distance between two people, the depth of a question, the weight of a silence that has learned to speak.

inscription: every distance you measure changes the distance you are
